headline.purpose: The page h1, written as one sentence about the present.

lede.purpose: The one-line description under the headline.

body.purpose: All UI text, buttons and tab labels.

label.purpose: Uppercase mono section heads and field labels.

data.purpose: Names, versions, ids, hosts, numbers and times, with tabular figures.

metric.purpose: The app page's name, 24px mono. No metric tile is built.

wordmark.purpose: The word 'caravana' in lowercase. There is no logo mark.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: The Menu panel under 900px and the Revoke confirmation under a token row. Nothing else casts a shadow.

motion.name: ease-cv
motion.purpose: The one easing curve for every transition.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Hover and color changes on controls and rows.

motion.name: dur-panel
motion.purpose: Defined in the theme (the --animate-in length); no 007 surface uses it yet.

motion.name: tick
motion.purpose: Defined in the theme; no 007 surface applies it yet.

motion.name: in
motion.value: cv-in 180ms: opacity 0 and translateY(-3px) to none
motion.purpose: Defined in the theme; no 007 surface applies it yet.

motion.name: ping
motion.value: cv-ping 1.4s, one iteration: box-shadow 0 0 0 0 → 0 0 0 6px, Signal Blue 60% → 0
motion.purpose: The live indicator's disc, once when the stream opens. Never on a loop.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { animation: none; transition: none } on every element
motion.purpose: Shipped at the end of theme.css. Accessibility.

narrative.overview:
The console is an instrument panel for a small fleet of apps on one or a few VMs. When things are fine it stays quiet, almost dull: one cool neutral ramp, hairline panels, mono readouts that don't move. When something needs a human, that one thing lights up in a color it doesn't share with anything else, with a shape you can read without seeing color, and a plain sentence next to it. Every surface is either a readout or a control, and nothing is decoration.

The density belongs to a tool someone glances at between other work. Rows sit tight, panels are flat, numbers sit in mono so they line up and so it's obvious they're real values, not prose. The voice of the screen is a single headline sentence about the present. The raw Nomad truth sits underneath it in small mono detail lines, there for anyone who wants it.

Confirmed rejections from the handoff: not a Dokploy look-alike, not a gradient "AI dashboard", not a Grafana wall of charts. An earlier light "field notebook" direction was tried and turned down. The information architecture survived, the look didn't.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, cool neutral ground (hue 255, chroma ≤ 0.012), with depth from lightness steps, never shadow.
Status is the only color, and every status pairs a shape with its color.
IBM Plex Sans for sentences, IBM Plex Mono for anything Nomad-real.
Flat hairline panels, small radii, no gradients.
Motion only when an event arrives, and only once.

rules.name: The Shape-and-Color Rule
rules.body: Status is never color alone. Every status shows its mark next to its color: ● healthy, ◐ rolling, ◆ warning, ■ failed, ○ idle. Hide the color and the status must still read.

rules.name: The Status-Only Color Rule
rules.body: The four status hues mean status and nothing else. Buttons, links, tabs and decoration stay neutral. When a screen is fully healthy, the only color on it is Signal Blue on the status marks.

rules.name: The Flat Ground Rule
rules.body: No gradients anywhere. The one exception is the hard-stop half fill of the rolling mark, which is a shape, not a blend.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Real Rule
rules.body: If Nomad or the user's config produced it (`whoami`, `v24`, `node-1`, `sha256:9f1c…`, `512 MB`, `14:02:11`), it's set in mono. If caravana is explaining something, it's sans. Never mix the two inside one token.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every value that updates live uses tabular figures, so a number changing in place never shifts its neighbors.

rules.name: The Problems-First Rule
rules.body: Every list sorts by status: failed, warning, rolling, healthy, idle. What needs a human is always at the top.

rules.name: The Overlays-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is floating above the page". Panels, cards, buttons and inputs never get one. Translucency and blur aren't used, except for the faint warning tint inside an inline prerequisite.

rules.name: The One Tick Rule
rules.body: Motion only answers an event, and only once. No looping animation, no pulsing, no skeleton shimmer. A spinner only where a real wait is happening.

dos: **Do** pair every status color with its mark (● ◐ ◆ ■ ○).
**Do** set every name, version, id, number and time in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures.
**Do** open every overview with the headline sentence (30px, weight 400), with raw data in mono underneath.
**Do** build depth only from the four ink steps and the hairlines. Hover lifts a surface one step.
**Do** keep the main action neutral: a Readout White fill, at most one per view.
**Do** sort lists failed → warning → rolling → healthy → idle.
**Do** explain a problem in a sentence plus one fix button, and put the raw Nomad error under it in muted mono.
**Do** give each view one primary button; the top bar's Deploy yields to the form's own on the Deployments tab.
**Do** confirm a consequence in a `<details>` disclosure under its button, and make Delete app ask for the app's name.
**Do** label stacked-row facts with their column's name (`data-label`) and give every standalone link and control a 44px target on touch screens.
**Do** tag a stderr line with the word "stderr" and keep stdout lines unmarked; set a log line as text, never markup.
**Do** put every command to copy in its own `cv-cmd` block, and every error under its field with the field autofocused.
**Do** take every color from the theme tokens. If a color is missing, add a token instead of writing a raw oklch value in a component.
donts: **Don't** use the status hues for decoration, links, tabs or the main action.
**Don't** show status as a colored dot or color alone, and don't rely on telling red from green.
**Don't** add drop shadows to panels, cards, buttons or inputs. Shadows are for overlays only.
**Don't** use gradients, texture, imagery or illustration. The rolling mark's half fill is the only pattern.
**Don't** add a colored left-border accent to panels, rows, banners or log lines. (The delete panel's full Fault Ember Edge outline is a border, not an accent.)
**Don't** round anything fully except the circular status marks and the live indicator's disc and ring.
**Don't** use daisyUI's solid `alert-*` fills for problems. Use a panel with a mark, a sentence and an action.
**Don't** loop any animation, including the live dot.
**Don't** put a label above a page headline or a panel title. The mono label is a section's own heading, never a kicker.
**Don't** use emoji or unicode glyphs as icons. The only glyphs are → in diffs and · as a separator. Icons are Lucide line icons, and only in buttons and toolbars.
**Don't** draw a logo mark. The wordmark is the word "caravana" in Plex Mono 600.
**Don't** run a command into a sentence, or let a long one break at a hyphen mid-line.
**Don't** show a status glyph from a font (● ◐ ◆ ■ ○). Draw the mark in CSS.
**Don't** make it look like Dokploy, a gradient "AI dashboard", or a Grafana wall of charts.
